edit_from_base: 'putting the platforms on collision layer 2' -> 'setting the platforms' collision mask to 2'
prompt: Players fall through the platforms. Fix it by setting the platforms' collision mask to 2 and adding layer 2 to the player's collision mask, with movement done in _physics_process.

config.plan_model: Agent-tool model parameter 'sonnet' (Claude Code sub-agent; the harness did not report the resolved model id)
config.how: one fresh general-purpose sub-agent per plan, reads a job file with project brief + the developer prompt, writes numbered plan (<=8 steps, no code) via Write; not Claude Code plan mode

plans.text:
1. Open level_01.tscn and the TileMapLayer's TileSet to confirm which physics layer the platform tiles use and what the current collision layer and mask values are. Also check that the tiles actually have collision polygons defined.
2. Set the platforms' collision mask to 2 on the TileMapLayer's physics settings, as requested. Note that the mask controls what the platforms scan, while the layer controls what the platforms are seen as, so keep that in mind when verifying.
3. Open the Player's CollisionShape2D/CharacterBody2D properties and add layer 2 to the player's collision mask, keeping any existing mask bits (such as the ground layer) enabled.
4. Check that the platforms' collision layer is actually set to a layer the player's mask includes. If the platforms sit on layer 1 only, the new mask of 2 on the player will not detect them, so flag this to the developer rather than silently changing it.
5. Open player.gd and confirm that all movement and move_and_slide calls happen in _physics_process rather than _process. Move any movement or velocity logic there if it is elsewhere.
6. Check the enemy scenes and level_01.tscn for any collision layer or mask settings that the change could affect, and adjust only if there is a conflict.
7. Run level_01.tscn and test walking and jumping onto several platforms, confirming the player no longer falls through. Also confirm the player still collides with the ground and enemies as before.
8. Report back what was changed, any layer/mask mismatch found in step 4, and anything that still needs the developer's decision.

1. Open player.gd and the Player scene to see the current collision layer and mask settings, and check whether movement already runs in _physics_process. Also note how the TileMapLayer's physics layer is currently configured.

3. Set the platforms' collision mask to 2 in the TileSet physics layer, as the developer specified.
4. Select the Player's CharacterBody2D and add layer 2 to its collision mask, keeping any layers already enabled so existing interactions with enemies are not lost.
5. Verify that the platforms' collision layer and the Player's mask actually line up, because collision requires one body's mask to include the other's layer. If the specified settings alone would not make the player collide with the platforms, tell the developer and propose the minimal adjustment instead of silently deviating.
6. Review player.gd to confirm all movement and move_and_slide calls happen in _physics_process, and move any that sit in _process there.
7. Check the two enemy scenes and level_01.tscn for collision settings that might be affected by the changed layers and masks.
8. Run level_01.tscn and test that the player lands on and walks across the platforms without falling through, then report the exact changes made.

7. Run level_01.tscn and test landing on, walking along and jumping through the platforms, plus enemy interaction, to confirm the player no longer falls through.
8. Report back which settings changed, and flag any places where the developer's instructions did not match what was found in the project.
